h: Repentance Transforms the Days of Evil

p: וַיְהִי מִקֵּץ שְׁנָתַיִם יָמִים.
— And it came to pass at the end of two years.
בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (קצג ב), רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר פָּתַח: חַי הַשֵּׁם וּבָרוּךְ צוּרִי וְגוֹמֵר, וּבָרוּךְ צוּרִי דָּא הוּא דִכְתִיב בָּרוּךְ הַשֵּׁם צוּרִי וְכוּלֵי.
— In the holy Zohar (193b), Rabbi Elazar opens: “Hashem lives, and blessed is my Rock,” and so forth. “Blessed is my Rock” is what is written, “Blessed is Hashem, my Rock,” etc.
תָּא חֲזֵי, כְּמָה דְאַתְּ אָמַר בָּרוּךְ אֲדֹנָי יוֹם יוֹם, בָּרוּךְ אֲדֹנָי בְּאָלֶ"ף דָּלֶ"ת נוּ"ן יוֹ"ד וְכוּלֵי. יוֹם יוֹם אֵלּוּ שְׁנָתַיִם יָמִים.
— Come and see, as it says, “Blessed is Adonai, day by day”—Adonai spelled alef, dalet, nun, yud, etc. “Day by day” refers to these two years.
דְּהִנֵּה הַשֵּׁם אֲדֹנָי מוֹרֶה עַל תּוֹקֶף הִתְגַּלּוּת הַיִּרְאָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְאִם אֲדוֹנִים אָנִי אַיֵּה מוֹרָאִי.
— The Name Adonai indicates a powerful revelation of awe, as it says, “If I am a Master, where is My fear?”
וְיִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם הוּא בְּחִינַת תְּשׁוּבָה לְתַקֵּן הֶעָבָר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ כַּמָּה פְעָמִים.
— Fear of Heaven is the aspect of repentance that rectifies the past, as we have said several times.

וּמִזֶּה בָּא תַּקִּיפוּת לְלֵב הָאָדָם, וְזֶהוּ דִכְתִיב בָּרוּךְ הַשֵּׁם צוּרִי, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ה ב): מָצִינוּ שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, דִּכְתִיב צוּר לְבָבִי וְחֶלְקִי אֱלֹהִים לְעוֹלָם.

— This gives strength to a person’s heart. That is “Blessed is Hashem, my Rock.” Shir HaShirim Rabbah (5:2) says that the Holy One, blessed be He, is Israel’s heart, as it is written, “God is the Rock of my heart and my portion forever.”
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹכֵן בְּלֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְהַיְינוּ שֵׁם אֲדֹנָי, בְּחִינַת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
— Hashem dwells in Israel’s heart. This is the Name Adonai, the aspect of the Congregation of Israel.

p: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְנוּ מֵהָרַב הַקָּדוֹשׁ זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה עַל פָּסוּק לִי דִבֶּר צוּר יִשְׂרָאֵל מוֹשֵׁל בָּאָדָם צַדִּיק מוֹשֵׁל יִרְאַת אֱלֹהִים.
— As we heard from the holy rabbi, of blessed and holy memory, concerning “The Rock of Israel spoke to me: He who rules over man is righteous, ruling in the fear of God.”
כִּי צוּר לְשׁוֹן תַּקִּיפוּת, וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נוֹתֵן תַּקִּיפוּת בְּלֵב הַבַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁדִּיבֵּר אֵלָיו בְּיִחוּד לִהְיוֹת מוֹשֵׁל בָּאָדָם צַדִּיק.
— “Rock” conveys strength: Hashem gives strength to the penitent’s heart, as though He had spoken personally to him, enabling him to rule over “man, the righteous one.”

הַיְינוּ גַּם בִּדְבָרִים שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ מֵרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק א ריט ב), יֵשׁ מֶמְשָׁלָה לְהַבַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה לְבַטֵּל זֹאת וּלְתַקֵּן.

— Even regarding matters about which Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai says in the holy Zohar that repentance does not avail, Heaven forbid (Zohar I, 219b), the penitent has the power to overturn that and effect rectification.
וְגַם מוֹשֵׁל בְּיִרְאַת אֱלֹהִים, מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר מִפִּי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא.
— He also “rules over the fear of God,” even over what has been spoken by the Holy One, blessed be He.
כְּעִנְיַן הַבַּת קוֹל שֶׁיָּצָא שׁוּבוּ בָנִים שׁוֹבָבִים חוּץ מֵאַחֵר, אַף עַל פִּי כֵן הָיָה בִּיכָלְתּוֹ לְתַקֵּן עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה מִפְּנֵי שֶׁכֵּן רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
— For example, although the heavenly voice declared, “Return, wayward children, except Acher,” he could nevertheless have rectified himself through repentance, for that is Hashem’s will.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּשְׁנֵי לוּחוֹת הַבְּרִית וּבְסֵפֶר רֵאשִׁית חָכְמָה שֶׁעַל זֶה רָמְזוּ (פְּסָחִים פו:): כָּל מַה שֶּׁיֹּאמַר לְךָ בַּעַל הַבַּיִת עֲשֵׂה, חוּץ מִצֵּא.
— Shnei Luchos HaBris and Reishis Chochmah explain that this is hinted at in Pesachim 86b: “Do everything the host tells you, except ‘Leave.’”

וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה יֵשׁ לְכַוֵּין מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ: בָּרוּךְ אֲדֹנָי יוֹם יוֹם, אֵלּוּ שְׁנָתַיִם יָמִים. הַיְינוּ שֶׁנּוֹתֵן תַּקִּיפוּת בְּלֵב הַבַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה לְתַקֵּן גַּם הַשְּׁנֵי יָמִים שֶׁנִּקְרָאִים יְמֵי רָע.
— In this light we may understand the Zohar’s interpretation of “Blessed is Adonai, day by day” as the two years: He gives the penitent strength to rectify even the two days called “days of evil.”

He answered: These are words of Torah, difficult to acquire like vessels of gold and fine gold, but easily lost like glass vessels. Acher told him: “Rabbi Akiva your teacher did not explain it that way. paragraphs.text: Shelah HaKadosh, Shenei Luchot HaBerit, Sha’ar HaOtiyot, Hilchot Biah 1:34: “The general principle is that there is nothing that cannot be repaired through repentance. What the Zohar explains as not depending on repentance means that his repentance is difficult; and this too is part of the difficulty of repentance: he is shown that repentance is of no avail. Nothing stands in the way of repentance. Even if you have heard, ‘Return, wayward children, except for so-and-so,’ as in the case of Elisha Acher, pay no heed. For Elisha Acher was ultimately accepted even though he did not repent; all the more so, had he repented, it would have helped him far more. Rather, the doors of repentance were closed before him, and he had to persist until the entrance opened. This is what our Sages said: ‘Do whatever the master of the house tells you, except “Leave.”’ The master of the house is the Holy One, blessed be He. Whatever He tells you to do among the commandments, do. ‘Except “Leave”’ means that if He tells you, ‘Leave My house and do not enter,’ as in the case of Elisha Acher, do not listen to Him; enter through repentance, for this is what the Holy One, blessed be He, desires, although He makes you think otherwise.”

h: Anger Desire and the Days of Evil

p: וּכְדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (קצח ב) עַל פָּסוּק לָמָּה אִירָא בִּימֵי רָע עֲוֹן עֲקֵבַי יְסֻבֵּנִי וְכוּלֵי: יְמֵי רָע וְאִלֵּין מְמַנָּן עַל אִינּוּן חוֹבִין דְּדָשִׁין בְּהוּ בְּנֵי נָשָׁא בְּעִקְבַיְיהוּ.

— The holy Zohar on this portion (198b) explains “Why should I fear in days of evil, when the sin of my heels surrounds me,” etc.: these “days of evil” are appointed over the sins people tread on with their heels.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁנִּדְמֶה בְּעֵינֵיהֶם שֶׁהוּא דָבָר קַל, וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר הוֹי מוֹשְׁכֵי הֶעָוֹן בְּחַבְלֵי הַשָּׁוְא וְכַעֲבוֹת הָעֲגָלָה חַטָּאָה.
— They regard such sins as insignificant. Of this it says, “Woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of falsehood, and sin as with wagon ropes.”
וְהַיְינוּ עַל שְׁנֵי הָעִנְיָנִים שֶׁנִּזְכַּר בַּגְּמָרָא שֶׁכָּךְ אוּמָנֻתּוֹ שֶׁל יֵצֶר הָרָע, הַיּוֹם אוֹמֵר לוֹ עֲשֵׂה כָךְ וְכוּלֵי, עַד שֶׁאוֹמֵר לוֹ וְכוּלֵי.
— This concerns the two matters for which the Gemara describes the evil inclination’s craft: today it tells him, “Do this,” etc., until eventually it tells him, etc.
וְנִזְכַּר בְּמִדַּת הַכַּעַס (שַׁבָּת קה:): הַמְקָרֵעַ בְּגָדָיו בַּחֲמָתוֹ וְכוּלֵי יְהֵא בְּעֵינֶיךָ וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁכָּךְ אוּמָנֻתּוֹ שֶׁל יֵצֶר הָרָע וְכוּלֵי.
— Concerning anger, Shabbat 105b says: “One who tears his garments in his rage,” etc., “should be regarded by you,” etc., “for this is the evil inclination’s craft,” etc.
וְגַם בְּמִדַּת הַתַּאֲוָה אִיתָא (נִדָּה יג:): דְּקָמְגָרֵי יֵצֶר הָרָע אַנַּפְשֵׁיהּ וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁכָּךְ אוּמָנוּת שֶׁל יֵצֶר הָרָע וְכוּלֵי.
— Concerning desire, too, Niddah 13b says that he incites the evil inclination against himself, etc., “for this is the evil inclination’s craft,” etc.
וְהַיְינוּ הַפְּסוֹלֶת שֶׁל שְׁנֵי יָמִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים שֶׁל הַבְּרִיאָה, שֶׁהֵם נֶגֶד הַמִּדּוֹת הַקְּדוֹשׁוֹת חֶסֶד וּגְבוּרָה.
— These are the impure offshoots of the first two days of Creation, which correspond to the holy attributes of kindness and might.

כִּי בַּיּוֹם הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת אַהֲבַת חֶסֶד, הֲגַם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ כִּי טוֹב, עִם כָּל זֶה מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָאוֹר נִגְנַז לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא, כִּי לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא יִתְלַבֵּן וְיִהְיֶה כּוּלּוֹ טוֹב.
— The first day embodies loving kindness. Although “it was good” was said of it, its light was nevertheless hidden for the future, when it will be purified and become entirely good.
אָמְנָם לְעֵת עַתָּה נִסְתָּעֵף מִזֶּה פְּסוֹלֶת אַהֲבָה זָרָה לְתַאֲוָה.
— For now, however, an impure offshoot branches from it: misplaced love expressed as craving.
וּבַיּוֹם הַשֵּׁנִי לֹא נֶאֱמַר כִּי טוֹב, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּבְרָא בּוֹ גֵיהִנֹּם, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַכַּעַס שֶׁאֵשׁ שֶׁל גֵיהִנֹּם שׁוֹלֵט בּוֹ.
— “It was good” was not said on the second day because Gehinnom was created then. It corresponds to anger, over which the fire of Gehinnom rules.

וְגַם מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּבְרָא בּוֹ מַחֲלוֹקֶת (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ד), וְכַעַס נוּרָא דְגֵיהִנֹּם כַּיָּדוּעַ (מִתִּקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּיקּוּן מח) עַל פָּסוּק לֹא תְבַעֲרוּ אֵשׁ בְּכֹל מוֹשְׁבֹתֵיכֶם.
— Also, discord was created on that day (Bereishis Rabbah, chapter 4). Anger is the fire of Gehinnom, as is known from Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 48, on “Do not kindle fire in any of your dwellings.”
וְזֶה מוֹרֶה שֶׁגַּם אִם נִמְשָׁךְ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם בִּשְׁנֵי הַפְּגָמִים, יֵשׁ קֵץ לִשְׁנֵי הַיָּמִים הָאֵלּוּ לְתַקְּנָם עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה.
— This teaches that even if, God forbid, someone is drawn into both blemishes, these two days have an end: they can be rectified through repentance.

paragraphs.text: Zohar I, 198b (Miketz 8:114–116): ““Joseph recognized his brothers, but they did not recognize him.” Rabbi Elazar opened: “Why should I fear in days of evil, when the iniquity of my heels surrounds me?” Come and see: there are three who fear without knowing what they fear, as has been explained. A person may fear without knowing why because of sins he does not recognize as sins and to which he pays no attention; he fears the days of evil. What are the days of evil? They are the days associated with that evil—the evil inclination, which is called evil. It has appointed days when it is given permission in the world to lead astray those who defile their ways; one who comes to defile himself is defiled. These are called days of evil, and they are appointed over the sins people trample with their heels. Come and see: many destructive bands encounter all who defile their ways, and defile them. A person is led along the very path he wishes to take. When a person comes to purify himself, many help him.”

paragraphs.text: Niddah 13b: “Rav said: One who deliberately arouses himself should be placed under a ban. Why not simply say that it is forbidden? Because he incites his evil inclination against himself. Rabbi Ami said: He is called a transgressor. Such is the evil inclination’s trade: Today it tells him, “Do this,” tomorrow, “Do this,” and eventually, “Go and worship an idol,” and he goes and does so. Some report Rabbi Ami’s statement this way: Whoever brings himself to sexual thoughts is not admitted into the Holy One’s presence. Here it is written, “It was evil in the Lord’s eyes,” and elsewhere, “For You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not dwell with You.” Rabbi Elazar said: What is meant by “Your hands are full of blood”? These are the people who commit adultery with their hands.”

h: Gain Through the Distress of Joseph

p: וְהִנֵּה אִיתָא בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה: בְּכָל עֶצֶב יִהְיֶה מוֹתָר, כָּל דָּבָר שֶׁנִּצְטַעֵר יוֹסֵף עִם אֲדוֹנְתּוֹ הָיָה לוֹ יִתְרוֹן מִמֶּנָּה, שֶׁנָּטַל אֶת בִּתָּהּ.
— Bereishis Rabbah interprets “In all distress there is gain”: through all the distress Joseph suffered with his mistress, he gained something from her, for he married her daughter.
וּדְבַר שְׂפָתַיִם אַךְ לְמַחְסוֹר: עַל יְדֵי שֶׁאָמַר לְשַׂר הַמַּשְׁקִים זְכַרְתַּנִי וְהִזְכַּרְתַּנִי נִיתּוֹסֵף לוֹ שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים.
— “But talk of the lips leads only to loss”: because he said to the chief cupbearer “remember me” and “mention me,” two years were added.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָמַר שָׁם: אַשְׁרֵי הַגֶּבֶר אֲשֶׁר שָׂם הַשֵּׁם מִבְטַחוֹ, זֶה יוֹסֵף, וְלֹא פָנָה אֶל רְהָבִים, עַל יְדֵי שֶׁאָמַר לְשַׂר הַמַּשְׁקִים וְכוּלֵי.
— It then says: “Happy is the man who makes Hashem his trust”—this is Joseph; “and has not turned to the arrogant”—because he said to the chief cupbearer, etc.
דְּהִנֵּה יוֹסֵף כַּאֲשֶׁר הֵבִיא אֶת דִּבָּתָם רָעָה אֶל אֲבִיהֶם לֹא הִרְגִּישׁ בָּזֶה שׁוּם חֵטְא בְּנַפְשׁוֹ.
— When Joseph brought an unfavorable report about his brothers to their father, he felt no sin within himself in doing so.
אָמְנָם כַּאֲשֶׁר נִמְכַּר לְעֶבֶד לְמִצְרַיִם וּבָאוּ לְפָנָיו הַנִּסְיוֹנוֹת, עַד שֶׁנָּגַע בּוֹ בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סוֹטָה לו:),
— But when he was sold as a slave to Egypt and confronted with trials, until the temptation touched his thoughts, as described in Sotah 36b,

וְאַחַר כָּךְ יָשַׁב בְּבֵית הָאֲסוּרִים עֶשֶׂר שָׁנִים, הִתְמַרְמֵר מְאֹד וּמִצְטַעֵר בְּנַפְשׁוֹ וְהָיָה עָצֵב מְאֹד עַל מַה שֶּׁעָלָה בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, שֶׁחַס וְשָׁלוֹם הָיָה לוֹ פְגָם וְחֵטְא גָּדוֹל בִּקְדוּשַּׁת הַבְּרִית, הֲגַם שֶׁנִּתְגַּבֵּר עַל יִצְרוֹ בְּפוֹעַל,

— and then he spent ten years in prison, he became deeply embittered and distressed. He grieved over the thought that had arisen, feeling that, Heaven forbid, he had gravely blemished the sanctity of the covenant, although in practice he had overcome his inclination.

וּלְבַסּוֹף הֶרְאוּ לוֹ שֶׁבְּכָל הָעֶצֶב שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ, שֶׁנִּצְטַעֵר עִם אֲדוֹנְתּוֹ, הַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁאֵירַע לוֹ בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה עָלֶיהָ שֶׁעַל זֶה נִצְטַעֵר מְאֹד, הָיָה לוֹ יִתְרוֹן מִמֶּנָּה שֶׁנָּטַל בִּתָּהּ.
— Ultimately, he was shown that all his distress involving his mistress—his intense grief over the thought of her—brought him a gain through her: he married her daughter.
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הָיָה לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת עִמָּהּ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה, שֶׁנּוֹלְדוּ לוֹ הַשְּׁנֵי שְׁבָטִים מִבִּתָּהּ, וְלָכֵן נָפַל לוֹ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה עָלֶיהָ.
— There truly was a holy connection between them, for her daughter bore him the two tribes; this is why the thought of her occurred to him.
וְגַם הִיא רָאֲתָה בָּאִצְטְרוֹלוֹגִין שֶׁלָּהּ, וְלָכֵן חָמְדָה לוֹ.
— She too perceived this in her astrology and therefore desired him.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים עַל אֵין אָרוּר מִדַּבֵּק בְּבָרוּךְ, שֶׁהָאָרוּר אֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה לִדָּבֵק בְּבָרוּךְ. וְרַק רְצוֹנָהּ וּתְשׁוּקָתָהּ הָיָה מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיָה לָהּ בֶּאֱמֶת אֵיזֶה שַׁיָּיכוּת אֵלָיו כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.

— As is said concerning “the cursed does not cleave to the blessed,” the cursed does not wish to cleave to the blessed. Her desire and longing arose only because she truly had some connection with him, as explained above.

h: Speech and the Need for Further Repair

p: אָמְנָם דְּבַר שְׂפָתַיִם שֶׁלּוֹ הָיָה אַךְ לְמַחְסוֹר, עַל יְדֵי שֶׁאָמַר לְשַׂר הַמַּשְׁקִים זְכַרְתַּנִי וְהִזְכַּרְתַּנִי.
— His “talk of the lips,” however, led only to loss, when he said to the chief cupbearer “remember me” and “mention me.”

וְזֶה לֹא נֶחְשָׁב בְּעֵינָיו לְשׁוּם חֵטְא, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת לֹא בָּטַח בְּשַׂר הַמַּשְׁקִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב אֲשֶׁר שָׂם הַשֵּׁם מִבְטַחוֹ זֶה יוֹסֵף; רַק לַאֲשֶׁר הִרְגִּישׁ שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת סִיבַּת תְּשׁוּעָתוֹ יִהְיֶה עַל יְדֵי שַׂר הַמַּשְׁקִים, רָצָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נַעֲשֶׂה הַיְשׁוּעָה עַל פִּי הַטֶּבַע, כִּי אֵין סוֹמְכִין עַל הַנֵּס.

— He regarded this as no sin at all. He truly did not trust the cupbearer—“who makes Hashem his trust” refers to Joseph—but sensed that his deliverance would come through him. He wished it to occur through natural means, since one does not rely on a miracle.

וְעִם כָּל זֶה הָיָה לוֹ לְמַחְסוֹר, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתּוֹסֵף לוֹ ב' שָׁנִים, לְעוֹרְרוֹ בָּזֶה עַל הַדְּבַר שְׂפָתַיִם שֶׁהֵבִיא דִבָּה עַל אֶחָיו שֶׁהָיָה נִדְמֶה לוֹ גַּם כֵּן שֶׁהוּא דָּבָר קַל.
— Nevertheless, it led to loss: two years were added, awakening him to his earlier “talk of the lips,” his unfavorable report about his brothers, which he likewise had regarded as insignificant.

וּבֶאֱמֶת נִסְתָּעֵף מִזֶּה שְׁנֵי הַפְּגָמִים הַנִּזְכָּרִים לְעֵיל, כִּי לָשׁוֹן הָרָע וְהוֹצָאַת דִּבָּה בָּא מִסִּבַּת קִנְאָה וְכַעַס, וּבְרִית הַלָּשׁוֹן מְכוּוָּן נֶגֶד בְּרִית הַמָּעוֹר כַּיָּדוּעַ.

— In truth, both blemishes mentioned above branch from this. Harmful speech and defamation arise from jealousy and anger; and the covenant of the tongue corresponds to the covenant of the procreative organ, as is known.

וּדְבַר שְׂפָתַיִם כָּאֵלּוּ הֵמָּה מֵעֲוֹנוֹת שֶׁאָדָם דָּשׁ בַּעֲקֵבָיו, וְהֵם אַךְ לְמַחְסוֹר, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתּוֹסֵף לוֹ ב' שָׁנִים לְעוֹרְרוֹ שֶׁנִּצְרָךְ לְתַקֵּן פְּגַם הַשְּׁנֵי יָמִים עַל יְדֵי הַדְּבַר שְׂפָתַיִם.

— Such speech is among the sins people tread on with their heels, and it leads only to loss. Two years were therefore added to awaken him to the need to rectify the blemish of the two days through addressing that speech.

וְעַל זֶה מְרַמֵּז וַיְהִי מִקֵּץ שְׁנָתַיִם יָמִים, הַיְינוּ כַּאֲשֶׁר נִתְקְנוּ פְּגַם הַשְּׁנֵי יָמִים כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, וּפַרְעֹה חוֹלֵם, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר עַד עֵת בֹּא דְבָרוֹ אִמְרַת הַשֵּׁם צְרָפָתְהוּ.

— This is hinted at by “And it came to pass at the end of two years”: when the blemish of these two days was rectified, “Pharaoh dreamed.” As it says, “Until the time that his word came, Hashem’s utterance refined him.”

Moshe Chaim Luzzatto, Mesillat Yesharim, ch. 4: “Joseph, because he said to the chief cupbearer, ‘But remember me when it is well with you,’ had two years added to him, as our Sages said. … In the chapter ‘All are obligated’ they said (Chagigah 5a): When Rabbi Yochanan reached this verse he would weep: ‘I will draw near to you for judgment, and I will be a swift witness.’ A servant whose light deeds are weighed against him like his grave ones, is there any remedy for him? Certainly the meaning is not that the punishment for both is the same, for the Holy One, blessed be He, pays only measure for measure. Rather, in the weighing of deeds the light ones rise on the scale just as the grave ones do, for the grave ones do not make the light ones forgotten, and judgment does not turn its eye from them at all, just as it does not turn it from the grave ones. For just as the Holy One, blessed be He, does not fail to reward any good deed, however small, so He does not fail to judge and reprove any bad deed, however small, to remove from the hearts of those who wish to be enticed the thought that the Master, blessed be He, will not bring the light matters into His judgment.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 20: “Rashi explained ‘Let us go to Dothan’ as seeking legal pretexts to put him to death; that is, they judged him liable to death by law, because he had testified to their father that they ate a limb from a living animal. … When he was cast into the pit of snakes and scorpions and they did not kill him, Joseph knew that they had been brought before him to kill him and that a miracle had been done for him. Then he sensed in his soul that he needed to be refined in the two matters: that he had spread a report about his brothers that they cast their eyes on the daughters of the land, and that they were suspected of eating a limb from a living animal. For it was for this that the snakes and scorpions confronted him: the snake is the root of the blemish of the covenant, the serpent’s counsel that it put into Adam through the craving of eating; and the scorpion surely kills, corresponding to the blemish of murder drawn from Cain, which corresponds to the blemish of a limb from a living animal, which even the nations avoid because it is great cruelty. … And after all this, when he was sold as a slave, it was made known to him that he still needed further refinement in this, for the blemish had not yet been fully repaired.”
